a.title: Resume-work compact header
a.mechanism: Keep the resume-work header and pending counts; use existing Start eligibility, show a concise disabled reason, keep historical period and inclusion scope visible, and retain named Summary, section Options and task Details. Start remains governed by existing eligible pending tasks.
a.visible: Empezar, list identity, period and pending tasks. Exact reference period and current inclusion scope remain readable.
a.disclosed: Resumen exposes full scope, diagnostic and estimates; section options and task details retain all properties, links and configuration. Retain every existing editor, action, link, diagnostic and scoped menu without duplicating command menus.
a.access: 44px Start, summary and detail controls; explicit disabled state when no pending reminders; visible focus. Minimum 44px targets; visible keyboard focus; no hover-only routes; wrap at 320/375px; scoped reduced motion.
a.benefit: Makes resumption immediate without requiring a scan of every metric.
a.risk: Starting must retain existing eligibility and section scope.
a.verification: Verify disabled Start, section versus page start, historical periods, mixed routines and metadata editing without changing sequence semantics.

b.title: Ledger with single material toolbar
b.mechanism: Retain the flat ledger and single glass toolbar; align named totals only where they fit, and stack supplemental field actions in an expandable line when width is constrained.
b.visible: Identity, completion, exact reference period, inclusion scope and relevant deadline; applicable labeled totals where readable.
b.disclosed: Supplemental task fields expose every original editor and link; toolbar and section controls retain scope, diagnostic, breakdown and unchanged menus.
b.access: Semantic 44px field controls, stable keyboard order, scoped names and visible focus; no horizontal ledger scrolling at 320px, with reduced motion.
b.benefit: Keeps substantial information visible without visual surface inflation.
b.risk: Many fields may require responsive column priorities.
b.verification: Check 320px field stacking, shopping exceptions, parallel versus active totals and focus targets.

a.title: Semantic one-line status replacement
a.mechanism: Replace duplicated progress indicators with one count-first status sentence that distinguishes own completion from included pending work using unchanged status calculations.
a.visible: Exact selected period, active inclusion scope, meaningful count sentence, task completion and relevant deadlines.
a.disclosed: The semantic status control opens the existing diagnostic; secondary disclosure preserves duration, inclusion and all task metadata; original menus stay separately scoped.
a.access: 44px status button, complete accessible name, wrapping count text, stable focus and keyboard access without duplicate spoken progress.
a.benefit: Removes redundant progress signals while keeping spoken information complete.
a.risk: A sentence may wrap differently as counts change.
a.verification: Test all_done, own-done/accumulated-pending, zero-goal and historical states; confirm diagnostic selectors and duration routes survive.

b.title: Period provenance captions
b.mechanism: Use one provenance caption per truly matching block, explicitly identifying view context; retain direct local disclosure for differing scope and recurrence.
b.visible: Exact selected period, active scope, counts, completion and differing task frequency or date context.
b.disclosed: Provenance exposes navigator, inclusion and diagnostic; task Details retains complete metadata and editors; existing Options stays locally available.
b.access: 44px captions that act as buttons, full contextual names, keyboard disclosure and focus return; wrap short local captions at 320px.
b.benefit: Shows where accumulated maintenance work comes from.
b.risk: Repeated provenance captions can be lengthy.
b.verification: Verify own/accumulated totals, mixed-frequency sections, custom cycles, reference dates and mobile wrapping.

a.title: One summary sentence
a.mechanism: Use one short context sentence with deadline precedence and explicit empty-data rules; wrap without truncation. Limit the synopsis to consequential context; no truncated period labels.
a.visible: Title/check, exact period, active inclusion, section count and deadline or estimate.
a.disclosed: A labeled Details button per object reveals count composition, estimates and all original metadata actions; page and section Options preserve complete menus and diagnostics.
a.access: 44px nonoverlapping targets, scoped labels, keyboard disclosure, visible focus/return, 320px wrapping and reduced motion.
a.benefit: Removes badge boundaries while keeping meaningful context.
a.risk: Sentence generation needs robust empty and mixed-data handling.
a.verification: Check no estimates, custom recurrence, prices with quantity, task links and historical rollover.

b.title: Inherited context line
b.mechanism: Print labeled shared context once per matching block; show all differing deadlines, recurrence and scope, and describe inherited context without changing task settings.
b.visible: Exact period, inclusion scope, titles/counts, completion and every meaningful context exception.
b.disclosed: Context exposes existing period navigation, inclusion and duration; task Details retains full original metadata and editors; Options preserves existing menus.
b.access: 44px contextual buttons, semantic exception text, explicit inherited-context descriptions, visible keyboard focus and wrapping at 320px.
b.benefit: Removes repeated information while making the source legible.
b.risk: Inherited context could be mistaken for a task's own setting.
b.verification: Verify differing frequencies, historical dates, same-period tasks, metadata editors and narrow wrapping.

a.title: Steady metadata rail
a.mechanism: Keep one stable summary rail below each title; use a simple Details label for sparse metadata and remeasure expansion. Re-measure virtualized rows when local details expand.
a.visible: Title, completion, exact period, active scope and wrapping summary.
a.disclosed: Rail opens all metadata with direct duration/price/date/frequency editing and time-of-day cycling; section/page rails expose breakdowns and scope controls. Preserve all existing data and callback semantics.
a.access: 44px nonoverlapping targets, scoped labels, keyboard disclosure, visible focus/return, 320px wrapping and reduced motion.
a.benefit: Stable control positions support fast scanning as data changes.
a.risk: Reserved rail space can waste room on sparse tasks.
a.verification: Verify empty metadata, changing completion/counts, subtask totals, menus and virtualized row sizing.

b.title: Three disclosure shelves
b.mechanism: Use independent Resumen, Alcance and Propiedades shelves at their relevant object level; preserve scope words and real local overrides beside closed summaries, with measured expansion.
b.visible: Exact period, active inclusion, local overrides, titles, completion and named shelf controls.
b.disclosed: Resumen retains diagnostic and duration routes; Alcance retains inclusion and breakdown; task Propiedades retains all metadata actions and links without duplicating menus.
b.access: 44px semantic shelf controls, independent section collapse, stable focus and measured virtualized heights; no hover-only access or horizontal overflow.
b.benefit: Keeps object scope local and makes hidden information predictable.
b.risk: Expanded shelves can lengthen the virtualized list.
b.verification: Measure shelf-height integration, 320px wrapping, inclusion toggles and completion without accidental shelf activation.

a.title: Context-first mobile folio
a.mechanism: Place a wrapping global context line before the task list in one column; repeat local captions only for real differences and retain meaningful deadlines next to their tasks.
a.visible: Exact period, inclusion scope, title/completion, counts and due exceptions.
a.disclosed: Full-width Details retains metadata actions and breakdowns; separate Options and inclusion controls preserve original commands and diagnostic routes.
a.access: 44px nonoverlapping controls, explicit local names, readable long Spanish captions, keyboard disclosure and focus return at 320px.
a.benefit: Readable context establishes meaning before dense titles.
a.risk: More lines may delay the first task on initial load.
a.verification: Test long list/section/task titles, historical dates, rollover and scrolling without stale captions.

b.title: Depth-independent context rows
b.mechanism: Keep hierarchy guides but place local context and Details outside deep indentation; bind each full-width context row to its adjacent heading and complete ancestor path.
b.visible: Hierarchy cue, local context, title/count, completion and exact global period/inclusion scope.
b.disclosed: Context exposes period, duration and inclusion; separate Options retains the original section menu; task Details preserves all editors and links.
b.access: 44px nonoverlapping controls, full ancestor labels, independent collapse and disclosure, visible keyboard focus and wrapping at 320px.
b.benefit: Metadata remains readable even at deep nesting.
b.risk: Reduced indentation can weaken parent-child recognition.
b.verification: Verify five-level nesting, screen-reader path, drag affordances, mixed periods and mobile widths.

a.title: Deadline action row
a.mechanism: Retain the dedicated deadline action row for meaningful due context, omit empty deadline rows, and keep full date editing in Details; header period, section scope, estimates, diagnostics and original commands remain available. Keep ordinary date editing reachable in Details even when no urgent row is shown.
a.visible: Completion target, title, urgent deadline in words, selected period and scope. Exact reference period and current inclusion scope remain readable.
a.disclosed: Deadline button invokes date editing; Details provides all other task actions; header Estimates/Options and section Scope/Options retain totals, diagnostics and commands. Retain every existing editor, action, link, diagnostic and scoped menu without duplicating command menus.
a.access: Use semantic buttons, 44px nonoverlapping targets, visible focus, keyboard disclosure, scope-specific names and focus return; disable scoped motion when requested. Minimum 44px targets; visible keyboard focus; no hover-only routes; wrap at 320/375px; scoped reduced motion.
a.benefit: Urgency is actionable and visually distinct from finishing the task.
a.risk: Two-row tasks use more vertical space.
a.verification: Test touching deadline versus checkbox, past-period overdue context and keyboard focus order.

b.title: Stable essential spine
b.mechanism: Retain the stable essential spine and inline definition lists; use object-specific accessible names, persistent selected period and inclusion state, separate completion targets, and existing Options menus with no hidden keyboard destinations. Keep completion separate and give every disclosure an object-specific name.
b.visible: Essential spine and nonredundant date exceptions; inclusion state always stated. Exact reference period and current inclusion scope remain readable.
b.disclosed: Details expands semantic definition lists containing every datum and original action; header/section summaries use the same disclosure pattern, with diagnostic and inclusion controls retained. Retain every existing editor, action, link, diagnostic and scoped menu without duplicating command menus.
b.access: Use semantic buttons, 44px nonoverlapping targets, visible focus, keyboard disclosure, scope-specific names and focus return; disable scoped motion when requested. Minimum 44px targets; visible keyboard focus; no hover-only routes; wrap at 320/375px; scoped reduced motion.
b.benefit: Predictable focus structure keeps minimalism operable.
b.risk: Many Details buttons need object-specific accessible names.
b.verification: Verify tab order, expanded state, focus ring, all commands and no invisible focus targets.

a.title: Persistent scope watermark
a.mechanism: Keep the persistent scope watermark as readable text and a 44px labelled scope button, show exact period nearby, and repeat only differing section scopes; its disclosure retains existing inclusion, estimate and diagnostic actions. Treat scope as explicit readable state, never a decorative watermark alone.
a.visible: Selected month, explicit own/combined scope text, titles and completion. Exact reference period and current inclusion scope remain readable.
a.disclosed: Watermark opens scope toggle with current state plus duration and diagnostic; task Details opens original metadata; list/section Options remains visible. Preserve all existing data and callback semantics. Retain every existing editor, action, link, diagnostic and scoped menu without duplicating command menus.
a.access: 44px watermark button, text rather than color signal, semantic state and keyboard access. Minimum 44px targets; visible keyboard focus; no hover-only routes; wrap at 320/375px; scoped reduced motion.
a.benefit: Scope survives even when supporting controls are disclosed.
a.risk: Too many differing scopes can repeat context.
a.verification: Verify section/global independence, own-done/accumulated-pending state, menus, dates and small widths.

b.title: Origin ledger
b.mechanism: Use a plain origin ledger naming shorter-frequency contributions; distinguish inclusion from overdue backlog. Never use overdue wording for frequency inclusion.
b.visible: Exact period, compact origin summary, active scope, titles, completion and due exceptions.
b.disclosed: Ledger expansion shows original routine breakdown, duration and diagnostic; section Details exposes inclusion; task Details retains all editors; Options preserves menus. Preserve all existing data and callback semantics.
b.access: 44px nonoverlapping targets, scoped labels, keyboard disclosure, visible focus/return, 320px wrapping and reduced motion.
b.benefit: Accumulated work stops looking like unexplained arithmetic.
b.risk: Source rows could be mistaken for overdue backlog.
b.verification: Verify labels match actual frequency accumulation, historical referenceDate, all-done states and widths.

a.title: Shape-and-text hierarchy
a.mechanism: Keep shape-and-text hierarchy with one glass navigation surface; let heading controls wrap underneath long names, state exact period and own/accumulated scope, and show concurrent calculations with explicit labels inside Summary. Use glass for navigation and opaque readable content fallback.
a.visible: Titles, exact period, completion shape/state and scope sentence. Exact reference period and current inclusion scope remain readable.
a.disclosed: Summary and details expose every statistic, property and command with labelled rows; diagnostics remain on the existing route. Retain every existing editor, action, link, diagnostic and scoped menu without duplicating command menus.
a.access: 44px controls, opaque contrast fallback, text labels for status and no color-only accumulated distinction. Minimum 44px targets; visible keyboard focus; no hover-only routes; wrap at 320/375px; scoped reduced motion.
a.benefit: Reduces optical clutter while preserving distinguishable controls.
a.risk: Extra text labels can consume narrow width.
a.verification: Compare light/dark/reduced-transparency screenshots at 320px; exercise accumulated status, estimates and completion.

b.title: One calm context tray
b.mechanism: Retain the calm context tray; show selected period and current inclusion scope in the closed tray, separate navigator and inclusion groups inside, and keep original summaries, diagnostics, menus and task editors reachable. Each scope and date control retains its independent callback and state.
b.visible: Title, selected period, scope label, completion and essential deadline. Exact reference period and current inclusion scope remain readable.
b.disclosed: Tray expands existing period navigator, accumulated switch, duration breakdown and diagnostic; list and section options retain named routes; task panel contains all metadata editors. Preserve all existing data and callback semantics. Retain every existing editor, action, link, diagnostic and scoped menu without duplicating command menus.
b.access: 44px buttons, semantic expansion, restored focus; keyboard access and opaque glass fallback. Minimum 44px targets; visible keyboard focus; no hover-only routes; wrap at 320/375px; scoped reduced motion.
b.benefit: A single stable place carries supporting information.
b.risk: Combining scope and date could imply they share state.
b.verification: Check independent scope/date callbacks, duration, menus, completion and 320/375px.

a.title: Named summary drawer
a.mechanism: Keep named summary drawers scoped by object; display exact period and inclusion beside their openers and a relevant compact estimate preview without duplicating management menus.
a.visible: Title, selected period, inclusion scope, completion and explicitly scoped Resumen/Detalles openers.
a.disclosed: Summary groups accumulated scope, estimates and diagnostics; task Details retains every editor and link; list and section menus stay separately named.
a.access: 44px semantic openers, labeled dialogs, keyboard focus trapping where modal, reliable focus return and readable wrapping at 320px.
a.benefit: Makes the next action obvious without requiring icon literacy.
a.risk: A drawer may add a step to planning.
a.verification: Complete a task; open scope and duration breakdown; change a historical period and edit every metadata field at 320px.

b.title: Measured wrapping priority
b.mechanism: Wrap by available content width using stable trigger nodes; adapt spacing and placement without replacing focused controls, open-panel launchers or their state.
b.visible: Title/completion, exact period, inclusion scope, counts and meaningful deadline exceptions.
b.disclosed: Details retains every metadata action; header and section summaries expose estimates and breakdown; diagnostics, inclusion and original menus remain reachable.
b.access: 44px nonoverlapping controls, stable DOM focus relationships, scoped labels, keyboard disclosure and 320px wrapping with reduced motion.
b.benefit: Responsive layout follows content pressure without trimming essential context.
b.risk: Threshold changes can cause distracting layout shifts.
b.verification: Resize with open menus and keyboard focus; test 320px/375px, long labels, reduced motion and selector preservation.

a.title: Exception gutter
a.mechanism: Keep the exception gutter on roomy layouts and stack one concise exception line on mobile; derive warnings from selected reference dates, retain accumulated origin where meaningful, and preserve all original data, editors, diagnostics and menus. Use selected reference dates rather than today's date for historical warnings.
a.visible: Titles, completion, selected period and explicit exceptional context. Exact reference period and current inclusion scope remain readable.
a.disclosed: Details reveal duration, frequency, price, links and time-of-day; header summaries open existing diagnostics and scope controls. Preserve all existing data and callback semantics. Retain every existing editor, action, link, diagnostic and scoped menu without duplicating command menus.
a.access: 44px named buttons and focus rings; exception text is never color-only. Minimum 44px targets; visible keyboard focus; no hover-only routes; wrap at 320/375px; scoped reduced motion.
a.benefit: Quiet everyday rows while retaining consequential differences.
a.risk: Too many exceptional tasks can refill the gutter.
a.verification: Test overdue, historical, partial and all-done states, metadata callbacks and mobile wrapping.

b.title: Outline with inline inspector
b.mechanism: Use an outline with closed local inline inspectors before section tasks; preserve independent collapse, measure expanded heights and avoid duplicate section menu routes.
b.visible: Headings/counts, exact period, active inclusion scope, title/completion and named Details openers.
b.disclosed: Local inspectors retain estimates, accumulated inclusion and the existing section Options; task Details retains metadata and links; global menu stays visible.
b.access: 44px semantic controls, independent disclosure and collapse, visible focus, measured virtualized expansion and readable nesting at 320px.
b.benefit: Supporting information stays beside the correct hierarchy node.
b.risk: Many open inspectors could become visually dense.
b.verification: Verify collapse/disclosure independence, virtualized sizes, all actions, referenceDate and 320px.

a.title: Reminder synopsis controls
a.mechanism: Use short scoped synopsis buttons with persistent chevrons; expand semantic detail locally and keep completion separate. Do not pack optional fields into the closed synopsis.
a.visible: Period/scope synopsis, section count/inclusion, task date/recurrence, title/check and Options.
a.disclosed: Synopsis expands its complete semantic detail block: dates, estimates, frequency, source list, price and links with original actions; routine diagnostic and inclusion remain available.
a.access: 44px nonoverlapping targets, scoped labels, keyboard disclosure, visible focus/return, 320px wrapping and reduced motion.
a.benefit: A visible reminder also provides a natural route to deeper information.
a.risk: Overloading synopsis text can obscure that it is interactive.
a.verification: Test chevron affordance, keyboard expansion, direct editors and completion remaining independent.

b.title: Native details groups
b.mechanism: Use native Details groups with scope-specific names outside clickable collapse regions; remeasure expanded rows and preserve independent section collapse and unchanged action callbacks.
b.visible: Titles, exact period, active scope, completion and named disclosure summaries.
b.disclosed: Opened groups retain inclusion, duration, diagnostics and every metadata editor/link; existing menus retain their original subjects and callbacks.
b.access: 44px native summaries, isolated events, visible keyboard focus, resilient text reflow and measured virtualized heights at zoom and 320px.
b.benefit: Uses predictable browser disclosure behavior with resilient text reflow.
b.risk: Virtualized list measurement must account for open details.
b.verification: Open nested groups at zoom, verify focus and heights, and test section collapse independently of metadata disclosure.

a.title: Exception-led metadata with stable details
a.mechanism: Suppress only safely redundant metadata; always show overdue/divergent dates and keep labeled Details stable at each scope. Unknown or divergent context remains visible; Details is always explicit.
a.visible: Completion, title, exceptional dates, exact selected period and active scope/filter context.
a.disclosed: All nonexception metadata remains in Detalles; page/section options and summary preserve every statistic and edit action.
a.access: 44px nonoverlapping targets, scoped labels, keyboard disclosure, visible focus/return, 320px wrapping and reduced motion.
a.benefit: Reduces repeated signals while keeping unusual obligations visible.
a.risk: A mistaken context comparison could suppress a needed date.
a.verification: Test mixed dates, overdue tasks, inherited frequencies and history; verify details always reveals complete values.

b.title: Stable focus emphasis
b.mechanism: Keep labeled controls fixed with adequate resting contrast; emphasize the focused containing row without revealing new commands or shifting layout.
b.visible: Completion, title, exact period, inclusion scope and visible Details/Options controls.
b.disclosed: Expanded summaries retain dense facts and original metadata actions; focused rows gain restrained contrast while all routes remain discoverable at rest.
b.access: 44px semantic targets, visible keyboard focus, adequate resting contrast for touch, stable control positions and reduced motion.
b.benefit: Helps users locate keyboard position in a restrained visual hierarchy.
b.risk: Overemphasis could turn every tab stop into visual noise.
b.verification: Tab through nested tasks and menus; compare unfocused/focused screenshots and ensure controls remain visible on touch.
